sanskrit_shloka:
जनक उवाच ॥
आकाशवदनन्तोऽहं घटवत् प्राकृतं जगत् ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥ ६-१॥
translation: Janaka said: I am infinite like space; the material world is like a pot within that space. Knowing this, there is neither renunciation, nor grasping, nor dissolution.

translations.author: English Translation
translations.text: Janaka said: I am infinite like space; the material world is like a pot within that space. Knowing this, there is neither renunciation, nor grasping, nor dissolution.

commentary_faqs.question: What do the metaphors of the pot and the ocean signify?
commentary_faqs.answer: They illustrate that the world (the pot or waves) has no independent existence apart from the Self (space or ocean), emphasizing the non-dual nature of reality.

commentary_faqs.question: Why does Janaka say there is no need for renunciation?
commentary_faqs.answer: Because the world is realized as a mere appearance or a wave of the Self; one cannot renounce or accept what is essentially oneself or an illusion.

sanskrit_shloka:
महोदधिरिवाहं स प्रपञ्चो वीचिसन्निभः ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥ ६-२॥
translation: I am like the vast ocean, and the world is like waves upon it. Knowing this, there is no renunciation, no grasping, and no dissolution.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहं स शुक्तिसङ्काशो रूप्यवद् विश्वकल्पना ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥ ६-३॥
translation: I am like mother-of-pearl, and the imagined world is like silver falsely superimposed upon it. Knowing this, there is no renunciation, no grasping, and no dissolution.

sanskrit_shloka:
अहं वा सर्वभूतेषु सर्वभूतान्यथो मयि ।
इति ज्ञानं तथैतस्य न त्यागो न ग्रहो लयः ॥ ६-४॥
translation: I am in all beings, and all beings are in me. Knowing this, there is no renunciation, no grasping, and no dissolution.
